concern.concern: Proof 3.3 bounds monochromatic consecutive windows only at levels ℓ < H, then concludes that “every search during one Johnson replacement then uses at most D=2s+1 entries per level.” This does not establish the bound at the highest level H: its initial traversal can visit the entire level-H list, and excluding long consecutive runs of promotion bits in level H−1 does not bound the total number of promoted nodes. Step 4.1 defines bad seeds solely by bucket occupancy and those run events, so the assertion that capped operations agree with ideal operations on every good configuration, subsequently used in 5.1–6.1, lacks this highest-level case. A separate highest-level occupancy argument is needed. I checked the cited Ambainis source, §6.2, PDF pp. 28–29 (https://arxiv.org/pdf/quant-ph/0311001); its consecutive-run discussion does not resolve this total-occupancy issue. This finding concerns the support supplied by the current proof, not a counterexample to the final asymptotic theorem.
